title: Comparison of large filtered presentations on small filtered subdiagrams
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; sets and indexing categories called small belong to $\mathcal U$, and all Hom sets are small. An infinite cardinal $\eta$ is regular when a union of fewer than $\eta$ sets of cardinality less than $\eta$ has cardinality less than $\eta$. A category is $\eta$-filtered when every diagram with fewer than $\eta$ morphisms admits a cocone; for a poset this means that every subset of cardinality less than $\eta$, including the empty subset, has an upper bound. An object is $\eta$-presentable when its Hom functor preserves small $\eta$-filtered colimits. Let $\sigma<\tau$ be infinite regular cardinals such that $a^b<\tau$ for all cardinals $a<\tau$ and $b<\sigma$. Let $\mathcal C$ be a locally presentable ordinary category: it has all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and, for some infinite regular $\eta$, is generated under small $\eta$-filtered colimits by a small family of $\eta$-presentable objects. Let $A,B$ be small $\tau$-filtered posets and $X:A\to\mathcal C$, $Y:B\to\mathcal C$ diagrams of $\tau$-presentable objects. Suppose that $\operatorname{colim}_A X$ and $\operatorname{colim}_B Y$ are isomorphic. For every pair of subsets $A_0\subseteq A$, $B_0\subseteq B$ of cardinality less than $\tau$, there exist subsets $A_1\subseteq A$, $B_1\subseteq B$ of cardinality less than $\tau$, each $\sigma$-filtered in its inherited order, containing $A_0$ and $B_0$ respectively, such that $\operatorname{colim}_{a\in A_1}X_a\cong\operatorname{colim}_{b\in B_1}Y_b$.

source.place: Lemma A.2.6.6, printed pp. 819-820, PDF pages 836-837 (zero-based), ordinary presentable categories and tau sharply above sigma. Read online; no Stacks tag states this comparison theorem.

proof.text: We first spell out the ordinary Hom-set calculation that will be used repeatedly. If $P$ is $\tau$-presentable and $(L,(z_i))$ is a colimit of a small $\tau$-filtered poset diagram $Z$, its defining preservation property says that $(\operatorname{Hom}(P,L),(h\mapsto z_i h))$ is a colimit of the sets $\operatorname{Hom}(P,Z_i)$. The index poset is nonempty and ordinarily filtered, since $\tau$ is infinite. Apply clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] to these sets. Every $h:P\to L$ factors as $z_i h_i$; and if $z_i h_i=z_j h_j$, there is $k\geq i,j$ with $Z(i\leq k)h_i=Z(j\leq k)h_j$. Thus factorization and equality detection use the original $\tau$-filtered presentation, never a smaller presentation that might fail to be $\tau$-filtered.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), element representatives and eventual equality after Definition 002V, applied to the Hom colimit from the definition of presentability.

proof.text: Choose a colimit $L$ of $X$ with legs $x_a:X_a\to L$. Compose the colimit cocone of $Y$ with the given isomorphism to obtain a colimit cocone with this same apex, with legs $y_b:Y_b\to L$. This remains colimiting: a cocone out of $Y$ factors uniquely through its original apex, and composition with the inverse isomorphism identifies such factorizations with maps out of $L$. Write $X_{aa'}$ and $Y_{bb'}$ for transition maps, and compose maps right to left. Local presentability supplies all the small colimits used here and in the last two steps.

source.place: Lemma A.2.6.6, printed pp. 819-820: common colimit; ordinary universal-property expansion by the worker.

proof.text: Here is the recursion invariant and its base. For ordinals $\xi<\sigma$ keep increasing subsets $S_\xi\subseteq A$, $T_\xi\subseteq B$, each of size less than $\tau$, starting with $S_0=A_0$, $T_0=B_0$. Also keep any factorization maps chosen at earlier stages, without changing them. At stage $\xi$, choose $u_\xi\in A$ above every element of $S_\xi$ and $v_\xi\in B$ above every element of $T_\xi$. These exist because the ambient posets are $\tau$-filtered and the two sets are $\tau$-small, including when they are empty. Put $P_\xi=S_\xi\cup\{u_\xi\}$ and $Q_\xi=T_\xi\cup\{v_\xi\}$. The next three steps prescribe the indices to adjoin to these two sets in forming $S_{\xi+1},T_{\xi+1}$. At a nonzero limit $\lambda<\sigma$ take the unions of the preceding sets and retain all previously chosen maps. Step 7 verifies the size invariant, so the recursion never asks for an unavailable upper bound.

source.place: Lemma A.2.6.6 and the transfinite back-and-forth idea of Lemma 5.4.6.3; explicit ordinary construction by the worker, base and invariant.

proof.text: For every $a\in P_\xi$ without an assigned factorization, apply Step 1 with $P=X_a$ to choose $\beta(a)\in B$ and $f_a:X_a\to Y_{\beta(a)}$ satisfying $y_{\beta(a)}f_a=x_a$. For every $b\in Q_\xi$ without an assigned factorization, choose $\alpha(b)\in A$ and $g_b:Y_b\to X_{\alpha(b)}$ satisfying $x_{\alpha(b)}g_b=y_b$. Keep assignments already made. Adjoin all $\beta(a)$ for $a\in P_\xi$ to $T_{\xi+1}$ and all $\alpha(b)$ for $b\in Q_\xi$ to $S_{\xi+1}$. Each application has $\tau$-presentable domain by the hypotheses on $X$ and $Y$, small Hom sets, and the original small $\tau$-filtered index poset. An index first added as a target need not have a factorization until a later stage.

source.place: Tag 04AX, stage representation, used through the Hom-set calculation of Step 1; ordinary back-and-forth factor choices.

proof.text: Impose compatibility for every comparable pair $a\leq a'$ in $P_\xi$. The maps $f_a:X_a\to Y_{\beta(a)}$ and $f_{a'}X_{aa'}:X_a\to Y_{\beta(a')}$ have equal composites to $L$, since both are $x_a$. Step 1, with presentable domain $X_a$, supplies $d\geq\beta(a),\beta(a')$ with $Y_{\beta(a)d}f_a=Y_{\beta(a')d}f_{a'}X_{aa'}$; adjoin this $d$ to $T_{\xi+1}$. For every $b\leq b'$ in $Q_\xi$, the corresponding calculation $x_{\alpha(b)}g_b=y_b=y_{b'}Y_{bb'}=x_{\alpha(b')}g_{b'}Y_{bb'}$ supplies $c\geq\alpha(b),\alpha(b')$ with $X_{\alpha(b)c}g_b=X_{\alpha(b')c}g_{b'}Y_{bb'}$; adjoin $c$ to $S_{\xi+1}$. These are equalities in actual diagram objects, not merely equalities after mapping to the total colimit.

source.place: Tag 04AX, eventual equality of two representatives, applied to Hom sets as in Step 1.

proof.text: Impose inverse identities whenever the needed factor maps are already assigned at this stage. For each $a\in P_\xi$ with $\beta(a)\in Q_\xi$, compare $g_{\beta(a)}f_a:X_a\to X_{\alpha(\beta(a))}$ with $1_{X_a}:X_a\to X_a$. Their composites to $L$ agree, because $x_{\alpha(\beta(a))}g_{\beta(a)}f_a=y_{\beta(a)}f_a=x_a$. Step 1 supplies $c\geq a,\alpha(\beta(a))$ with $X_{\alpha(\beta(a))c}g_{\beta(a)}f_a=X_{ac}$; adjoin $c$ to $S_{\xi+1}$. For each $b\in Q_\xi$ with $\alpha(b)\in P_\xi$, the equality $y_{\beta(\alpha(b))}f_{\alpha(b)}g_b=x_{\alpha(b)}g_b=y_b$ supplies $d\geq b,\beta(\alpha(b))$ with $Y_{\beta(\alpha(b))d}f_{\alpha(b)}g_b=Y_{bd}$; adjoin $d$ to $T_{\xi+1}$. Requirements whose target has not yet appeared are handled when it does appear; no inverse map is presumed before it has been chosen.

source.place: Tag 04AX, eventual equality, applied to the two composite-versus-identity comparisons.

proof.text: Define $S_{\xi+1}$ to be $P_\xi$ together with all indices in $A$ prescribed in Steps 4-6, and define $T_{\xi+1}$ analogously. To check the induction, put $\theta=\max(\aleph_0,|P_\xi|,|Q_\xi|)<\tau$; the inequality uses $\tau>\sigma\geq\aleph_0$. There are at most $\theta$ factor choices and inverse tests and at most $\theta^2=\theta$ comparable-pair tests, using the square clause of [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-square-power]. Each test adds one index, so both successor sets have cardinality at most a finite multiple of $\theta$, hence less than $\tau$. At a limit $\lambda<\sigma$, there are fewer than $\tau$ previous sets, each of size less than $\tau$, and regularity of $\tau$ bounds their unions. Previously assigned maps agree on their common domains because no assignment is ever changed. This verifies the invariant at the base, successors and limits and completes the indicated transfinite recursion. The choices are over small sets of indices, tests and Hom elements.

source.place: Cardinal.mul_eq_self, line 45 (square clause of the cited node); ordinary transfinite bookkeeping using the regularity assumed in the item.

proof.text: Set $A_1=\bigcup_{\xi<\sigma}S_\xi$ and $B_1=\bigcup_{\xi<\sigma}T_\xi$. They contain the prescribed subsets. Regularity of $\tau$ and $\sigma<\tau$ give $|A_1|,|B_1|<\tau$. For any subset $E\subseteq A_1$ of size less than $\sigma$, choose for each of its elements a stage containing it. Regularity of $\sigma$ bounds these fewer than $\sigma$ ordinals by some $\xi<\sigma$, so $E\subseteq S_\xi$; then $u_\xi\in S_{\xi+1}\subseteq A_1$ bounds $E$. For $E=\varnothing$ use $u_0$. The identical argument with $v_\xi$ proves $\sigma$-filteredness of $B_1$. All successor stages mentioned remain below the infinite initial ordinal $\sigma$. Every final index receives a factorization at some stage; its target is adjoined at the next stage. Every comparable pair eventually occurs together in some $P_\xi$ or $Q_\xi$, and every inverse test eventually has both required indices present. Thus every witness required in Steps 5 and 6 belongs to the final subsets. This includes $\sigma=\aleph_0$, when only finite sets need upper bounds.

source.place: Lemma A.2.6.6, required size and filteredness conclusions; worker expansion of the transfinite construction using regularity.

proof.text: Choose restricted colimits $U=\operatorname{colim}_{a\in A_1}X_a$ and $V=\operatorname{colim}_{b\in B_1}Y_b$, with legs $\widetilde x_a$ and $\widetilde y_b$. They exist since both subsets are small and $\mathcal C$ is cocomplete. For $a\leq a'$ the witness $d\in B_1$ of Step 5 and the cocone relations give $\widetilde y_{\beta(a)}f_a=\widetilde y_dY_{\beta(a)d}f_a=\widetilde y_dY_{\beta(a')d}f_{a'}X_{aa'}=\widetilde y_{\beta(a')}f_{a'}X_{aa'}$. Hence these maps form a cocone and the universal property gives $F:U\to V$ with $F\widetilde x_a=\widetilde y_{\beta(a)}f_a$. The witnesses for $b\leq b'$ similarly give a cocone and $G:V\to U$ with $G\widetilde y_b=\widetilde x_{\alpha(b)}g_b$.

source.place: Tag 002F (definition-colimit), induced maps from compatible cocones; the compatibility witnesses were constructed in Step 5.

proof.text: For $a\in A_1$, use the witness $c\in A_1$ of Step 6 to calculate $GF\widetilde x_a=\widetilde x_{\alpha(\beta(a))}g_{\beta(a)}f_a=\widetilde x_cX_{\alpha(\beta(a))c}g_{\beta(a)}f_a=\widetilde x_cX_{ac}=\widetilde x_a$. Uniqueness in the colimit universal property gives $GF=1_U$. For $b\in B_1$, its witness $d\in B_1$ gives $FG\widetilde y_b=\widetilde y_{\beta(\alpha(b))}f_{\alpha(b)}g_b=\widetilde y_dY_{\beta(\alpha(b))d}f_{\alpha(b)}g_b=\widetilde y_dY_{bd}=\widetilde y_b$, hence $FG=1_V$. Therefore $F$ is an isomorphism with inverse $G$, proving the claimed restricted-colimit comparison. No cancellation of a map to $L$ occurs in this argument.

source.place: Tag 002F (definition-colimit), uniqueness of maps out of a colimit, applied to the inverse witnesses of Step 6.
